LXP vs LMS: Key Differences Explained

A Learning Experience Platform (LXP) is a modern learning management system designed to offer a more personalized and engaging learning experience for users. Unlike traditional LMS platforms that focus primarily on delivering structured training content, LXPs prioritize the learner's experience by providing a curated and dynamic learning environment. One of the key features of an LXP is its ability to combine learning content from various sources, including internal digital assets, external third-party material, and even user-generated content. This diverse range of content ensures that learners have access to a wide array of resources to support their learning goals.

When I select an aggregate device under Sound in the Mac/OS menu bar, there is no volume slider. How do I control the volume?
When I select an aggregate device under Sound in the Mac/OS menu bar, there is no volume slider. How do I control the volume?

Short answer: macOS has no master volume for an aggregate device. Because it combines several devices, there is no single volume for the Sound menu slider or the volume keys to change. Set the level downstream of macOS instead: in the app or DAW, on the interface's own knob, per channel in Audio MIDI Setup, or with a third-party volume tool.
When I select an aggregate device under Sound in the Mac/OS menu bar, there is no volume slider. How do I control the volume?

Why it happens: Answer/Official from Create an Aggregate Device to combine multiple audio devices: an aggregate device merges the inputs and outputs of several devices into one device, for example an eight-channel and a two-channel device into one ten-channel device. Users report the same missing slider for aggregate and multi-output devices on Apple Community.
When I select an aggregate device under Sound in the Mac/OS menu bar, there is no volume slider. How do I control the volume?
When I select an aggregate device under Sound in the Mac/OS menu bar, there is no volume slider. How do I control the volume?
In the app or DAW. This is the usual route for music work. Ableton Live, Logic Pro and similar apps send audio to the aggregate device's outputs, so the master fader sets the level.
When I select an aggregate device under Sound in the Mac/OS menu bar, there is no volume slider. How do I control the volume?

On the hardware. Most audio interfaces control output level with an analog knob after the converter, so macOS cannot set their volume even when you use them on their own. Use the monitor or headphone knob.
When I select an aggregate device under Sound in the Mac/OS menu bar, there is no volume slider. How do I control the volume?

Per channel in Audio MIDI Setup. Select a member device (not the aggregate) in the Audio Devices sidebar, open its Output tab, and drag the channel sliders. This works only for devices whose driver exposes software volume, such as built-in speakers. On many interfaces the sliders are greyed out.
When I select an aggregate device under Sound in the Mac/OS menu bar, there is no volume slider. How do I control the volume?
Third-party tools. SoundSource sets per-app and per-device volume. MultiSoundChanger is an open-source menu bar app that changes the volume of every device in an aggregate device.
When I select an aggregate device under Sound in the Mac/OS menu bar, there is no volume slider. How do I control the volume?
If you only need to play to several outputs at once: that is a multi-output device, not an aggregate device (Apple guide). It has the same volume limitation, so the options above still apply.
